subject: Clarify: deconflating minimum billing vs. stitched long-context calls
messages:
From: Jack Liu <jack@acmehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwoodai.com>
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: How minimums apply to stitched long-context calls

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Finance asked me to clarify one thing before we move forward with the PO: how Redwood’s per-call minimums interact with our server-side stitching of very long conversation histories.

Background: we end up performing stitching on our side to produce a single long prompt (often 8k–12k tokens) that gets sent as one model call. Other times we send shorter incremental calls and stitch on the service side. Attached is a sample export of our daily usage (Acme_Usage_Sample.csv).

Questions:
- If we send a single 10k-token call, does that count as one call for the minimum (i.e., one minimum bucket), or multiple buckets aligned to your context slabs?
- When Redwood stitches multiple short calls into a single model invocation (for cache/KV reuse), do you still charge the per-call minimum for each original request, or for the final stitched call only?

We want to avoid a surprise uplift when the minimums are applied to our workload shape. Any concrete examples or a short math walk-through would help our procurement team.

Best,
Jack
Director of Platform Finance
AcmeHealth

Attachments: Acme_Usage_Sample.csv (csv)
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwoodai.com>
To: Jack Liu <jack@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2025-06-02T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: How minimums apply to stitched long-context calls

Jack —

Short answer up front: we bill minimums per model invocation that reaches the runtime, not per upstream request. If your integration sends one 10k-token request that is executed as a single runtime invocation, that counts as a single minimum bucket (and would be billed under the slab that covers 10k tokens). If you send three separate 3.5k requests and the runtime executes them separately, each will be evaluated against the minimum.

A couple of clarifications and an example:

1) Minimums and slabs
- We have per-invocation minimum behavior and context-slab sizing. For customers on enterprise SKUs (like the draft we discussed) the default internal policy is: per-invocation minimum = 50 tokens, and context slabs are applied for sequences longer than the model’s base window (we negotiate slabs for very long-context cases).

2) Server-side stitching / KV reuse
- If Redwood’s runtime receives multiple upstream fragments but consolidates them into a single model call (i.e., we do the stitch before the kernel execution because of prefix concat or KV aggregation), we bill that as a single invocation.
- If your client sends multiple independent calls that are executed independently (no server-side stitch), we evaluate each against the per-call minimum.

Concrete math (based on your attachment):
- Example day (from your file): 18,200 invocations, average request size 66 tokens, 120k tokens/day total.
- With a 50-token minimum per invocation you’d be billed for max(66,50) * 18,200 = 1,201,200 tokens (no surprise here).
- If a portion of your traffic is long stitched calls (say, 1,200 calls of 10k tokens) and those are sent as single invocations: billed as 1,200 * 10,000 = 12,000,000 tokens.

Proposal to avoid sticker shock
- We can offer a temporary pilot amendment: for the first 90 days post-PO, we will:
  a) Treat any server-side stitch that reduces upstream invocations into a single runtime call as a single invoiced invocation for minimums.
  b) Reduce the per-invocation minimum to 25 tokens for all Acme test traffic on the pilot.

Next steps: if that approach sounds acceptable I’ll loop in Jordan to draft the amendment and Karthik for pricing confirmation. I attached a one-page proposal (redwood-minimums-proposal-ACME.pdf) with the pilot terms.

—Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-minimums-proposal-ACME.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwoodai.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2025-06-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RE: How minimums apply to stitched long-context calls (internal)

Team — quick internal note on feasibility and economics before we sign anything:

1) Feasibility- Treating server-side stitches as a single runtime invocation is fine technically; our logs already show the final kernel invocation and that’s what the metering pipeline uses. We just need to be explicit in the SOW language ("metering keyed by runtime invocation id") so Finance has an audit trail.

2) Economics / example for Acme- Using Olga’s numbers:
  - Baseline monthly (30 days) from Jack’s sample: ~3.6M tokens (120k * 30).
  - If 1,200 long calls/day @10k tokens -> 12M tokens/day from those alone — looks like that was an example slice, not reality. We should confirm the actual fraction.

3) Concession limits- We can accept the 25-token pilot minimum for 90 days, but we should:
  - Cap cumulative waived-minimum exposure at $6k for the pilot (finance agreement).
  - Require Acme to sign the amendment + agree to share a daily usage CSV for reconciliation.

4) Pricing tweak suggestion- If procurement pushes back on the cap, offer instead a 30% discount on minimum-borne tokens (not on whole invoice) for the first two billing cycles. That’s easier for billing automation.

If you want I’ll draft the exact language for the amendment and a short reconciliation spreadsheet column set we’ll need.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Operations
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwoodai.com>
To: Jack Liu <jack@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodai.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwoodai.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2025-06-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: How minimums apply to stitched long-context calls — pilot terms and next steps

Jack —

Thanks for the clear question and for the sample file. We pulled the team together and propose the following concrete pilot amendment to be appended to the SOW:

Pilot amendment (90 days)
- Metering key: minimums will be applied per runtime invocation id (the kernel execution), not per upstream request. Server-side consolidation that results in a single kernel execution will be billed as one invocation.
- Minimum: lowered to 25 tokens per runtime invocation for the pilot period.
- Exposure cap: Redwood will cap waived-minimum credits at $6,000 total for the 90 day pilot.
- Reconciliation: Acme will provide a daily CSV (sample columns in the attached spreadsheet); Redwood will run a weekly reconciliation and credit any overages arising from minimum-billing differences.
- Optional alternate: if you prefer no exposure cap, we can instead apply a 30% discount on minimum-borne tokens for the first two billing cycles (we’ll calculate discount line items automatically).

Next steps:
1) Tell me which option you prefer (cap + 25-token minimum, or 30% discount on minimums).
2) If cap route chosen: sign the short amendment (DocuSign link below) and send the first daily CSV by June 7th.
3) We’ll set up a 30-minute weekly reconciliation call for the pilot cadence.

DocuSign (amendment): https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcd-efgh-ACME-SOW
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Happy to hop on a short call if procurement wants a one-page illustration for their legal/finance team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

--
Olga noted the pilot term and attached the redwood-minimums-proposal-ACME.pdf for the legal SOW language.
summary: Acme asked whether per-call minimums apply to stitched long-context requests. Redwood clarified metering is keyed to runtime invocation; proposed a 90-day pilot lowering per-invocation minimum to 25 tokens and capping waived credits at $6k, with an alternate 30% minimum discount. Next step: customer selects option and signs amendment via DocuSign.
